answeredReview: Review 5730474273, CHANGES_REQUESTED at ec13b8bb507abac20cb7496c0bf0ff53da6c944e, three inline findings. All three are fixed in commit 80bc419e9d9b055b7700b846299fca2e1bd7f6ed, answered on their threads and resolved.

proof.criterion: Round 2's finding: the control must not fail at random. /jsz names the new JetStream meta leader before that leader writes 'Self is new JetStream cluster metadata leader', so a single read of the log after the wait can miss it (the reviewer measured 1 of 15 probe runs, the line arriving 20 ms later).
proof.surface: The live test as the envoy-infra-go lane runs it, under the natslive tag, in the INFRA-961 issue pod: the count now runs inside the bounded within at clusteredhub_live_test.go:1198, so the wait ends only once that server has logged its election since the kill.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy/infra && TMPDIR=/legion/scratch/tmp go test -tags natslive -run '^TestClusteredNatsHubCluster$' -count=20 -timeout 180m -v ./gcp/ > /legion/scratch/tmp/infra961-r2-after.log 2>&1; grep -c -- '--- PASS: TestClusteredNatsHubCluster' /legion/scratch/tmp/infra961-r2-after.log; grep -c -- '--- FAIL' /legion/scratch/tmp/infra961-r2-after.log; grep -c 'led both LIVE_R3 and the JetStream meta group' /legion/scratch/tmp/infra961-r2-after.log
proof.observed: ok github.com/sjawhar/envoy/infra/gcp 680.920s; 20 '--- PASS: TestClusteredNatsHubCluster', 0 '--- FAIL', 20 lines naming 'led both LIVE_R3 and the JetStream meta group'. In 14 of the 20 runs the new meta leader was not the new stream leader, and the meta leader arrived 0.001-1.570 s after the stream leader (stream election 4.815-7.844 s after the kill, meta election 4.819-7.846 s).
proof.negativeControl: In a throwaway jj change, abandoned after the run, selfElected was set to 'Self is new JetStream cluster metadata leader (NEGATIVE CONTROL)', a line nats-server never writes, so the /jsz agreement alone would have passed the wait. The run was refused instead: 'clusteredhub_live_test.go:1199: a new JetStream meta leader after the SIGKILL, with its own election in its log: not within 30s: envoy-nats-0, which the survivors name the new JetStream meta leader, has not logged "Self is new JetStream cluster metadata leader (NEGATIVE CONTROL)" since the kill' (/legion/scratch/tmp/infra961-r2-control.log). jj --ignore-working-copy diff --stat reports 0 files changed afterwards.

proof.criterion: The fix the issue asks for still holds at the new head: every run kills the server that leads both the LIVE_R3 stream and the JetStream meta group, and js.StreamInfo and js.GetMsg run only once both survivors name one live meta leader.
proof.surface: The same live test: three real nats-server v2.15.1 processes on the chart's rendered nats.conf and auth.conf, started by the test in the issue pod with TMPDIR=/legion/scratch/tmp.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy/infra && TMPDIR=/legion/scratch/tmp go test -tags natslive -run '^TestClusteredNatsHubCluster$' -count=20 -timeout 180m -v ./gcp/ (the same run; the require.Equal before the kill and the wait before the reads fail the test when either does not hold)
proof.observed: 20 of 20 runs green, each with the (b) line 'SIGKILL of <server> (pid N), which led both LIVE_R3 and the JetStream meta group ...', and each with both survivors still naming the killed server as meta leader 3-5 ms after the kill.
proof.negativeControl: From round 1 and unchanged: in a throwaway jj change a second survivor is killed, so the lone server has no quorum, and js.GetMsg(LIVE_R3, 1) is refused 'code 503, err_code 10008, description "JetStream system temporarily unavailable"' 8.411 s after that kill. That is the refusal this wait avoids.

proof.criterion: The envoy-infra-go lane's static checks pass at the new head, and the committed test keeps one run per job (CI decides the lane itself).
proof.surface: The lane's own commands from packages/envoy/infra, as .github/workflows/ci.yaml lines 2469-2488 run them.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy/infra && gofmt -l gcp/clusteredhub_live_test.go && go vet -tags pulumilive,natslive ./...
proof.observed: gofmt -l printed nothing (exit 0); go vet -tags pulumilive,natslive ./... exited 0. The lane's live command was run at the round-1 head and reported only this pod's own gaps, which are unchanged: gcp's two data-disk tests need mkfs.ext4, and core's TestDispatchPermissionsOnRealServers and seed's TestAGeneratedSeedReachesNATS need a Docker daemon the pod does not run. None is in the file this change touches.
proof.negativeControl: The negative control above is also the build's: the deliberately wrong selfElected compiled and ran and the test refused it, so these commands do compile and exercise the file under test rather than skipping it. Without -tags natslive the file is not compiled at all and the run reports 'no tests to run'.

trickyParts: The control is now a condition of the wait rather than an assertion after it, so the wait ends on three facts at once: both survivors name one live leader, that leader is not the killed server, and that leader has logged its election since the kill. A line that never comes is the wait's timeout, which names the server and the missing line.

metaElected is still time.Since(killedAt) taken after the wait, so it now also covers the log line's arrival. The measured spread did not move: 4.819-7.846 s after the kill across 20 runs, against 4.371-8.572 s at the round-1 head.

The three outcomes of jsStreamLeaderStepDownRequest were read in the pinned source: js.isLeaderless() refuses 503/10008 at server/jetstream_api.go:2282-2286, before the stream checks at :2315-2319 and :2322-2324.
deviations: The reviewer's snippet kept the within's name as it was. The name now reads 'a new JetStream meta leader after the SIGKILL, with its own election in its log', so a timeout says which of the two facts was missing; the negative control's output shows that wording.
